events.content:
`UserDashboard` is now an async server component that fetches `https://api.example.com/user/preferences` fresh on every request and shows the results. The type check and production build both pass, and the build lists `/` as `ƒ (Dynamic)`, meaning it's rendered per request. I haven't called the real API; `api.example.com` is a placeholder. **`app/UserDashboard.tsx`** follows the pattern already in `app/page.tsx`: a helper function wrapped in try/catch, called from an async default component. Following the Next.js docs bundled with the project: - **`await connection()`** runs before the fetch, so the component waits for a real request and is never built ahead of time. It sits outside the try/catch so the error can't swallow it. - **`cache: 'no-store'`** is set on the fetch. Without it, Next.js in this setup fetches once during `next build` and reuses that result for everyone. - **`unstable_rethrow(err)`** is called in the catch. Otherwise the try/catch could swallow the error Next.js uses to switch to per-request rendering, and the page would quietly be built once with the fallback data. - It lists the returned preferences as key/value pairs, and shows "Unable to load your preferences right now." if the request fails. **`app/page.tsx`**: I wrapped `` in `Loading your dashboard...

}>` so the rest of the page shows right away while the preferences load. Checks: - `npx tsc --noEmit`: passed, exit 0. - `npx next build`: passed, exit 0. Two side effects of the build: - It rewrote `tsconfig.json`; I undid that with `git checkout -- tsconfig.json`. - It left untracked files: `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. I didn't touch your existing changes to `package.json` or the other untracked files. Because the page now renders on every request, the existing `/stats` fetch in `page.tsx` also runs each time instead of once at build. If that data should be cached, it would need `cache: 'force-cache'` or a revalidate option.
